title: bn254-gt-dlp: measured 32-adding rho in the Fp2/Fp6/Fp12 tower, 2^130.799212

claims.statement: For the full-production bn254-gt-dlp target, the single-trial 32-adding Pollard-rho algorithm of proof.md returns x with g^x=z with success probability at least 0.85 over uniform challenges and fresh algorithm coins, and every run performs at most W < 2^130.799212 units, where one unit is C=20,000 scalar AArch64 instruction equivalents. The per-step price 52,000 instructions is a 1.1007x charge over the Valgrind Callgrind measurement (47,239.44 Ir) of the shipped scalar C tower implementation. The work cap counts the 3N walk steps (N=2*ceil(sqrt(r))), N Floyd comparisons, all setup and table construction, recovery, verification and output; no work is amortised and no preprocessing is free. Success relies on the disclosed standard r-adding random-map heuristic, supported by the union-bound repeat probability and the 32-adding correction; it is not an unconditional theorem at production size.

experiments.purpose: Recompute every ledger row from the profile order, check the declared rational is the rounded-up log2(W), check the 0.85 success bound, and run the same 32-adding walk with Floyd detection on small prime additive groups as scope-limited correctness and statistics evidence.
